_meta.description: Document-rules config for writ_petition_criminal — Writ Petition (Criminal) WP(CRL) under Article 226 of the Constitution. Reliefs include illegal detention, custodial torture, FIR registration refusal, departmental misconduct in investigation, CBI/SIT transfer.
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. D.K. Basu, Lalita Kumari, Nilabati Behera cites mandatory.

title: Writ Petition (Criminal) under Article 226 of the Constitution of India

mandatory_clauses.description: Where misconduct rather than quashing sought

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {petitioner_name}, son/daughter/wife of {petitioner_father_name}, aged about {petitioner_age} years, resident of {petitioner_address}, the Petitioner herein, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above petition are true and correct to my personal knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Petitioner

promptInstructions: Draft a Writ Petition (Criminal) under Article 226. DISTINGUISH from S.528 BNSS quashing: quashing targets FIR/proceedings; WP(CRL) targets misconduct, refusal to investigate, compensation, SIT/CBI transfer, custodial wrongs.
Cause-title MUST include three-tier 'In the matter of' format: (1) Article 226 read with Article 21, (2) BNSS, (3) grievance summary, (4) parties.
Para 1: Description of parties. Where petitioner not the victim (e.g., relative), state relationship and authority to sue as next friend.
Para 2: Jurisdiction — cause of action territorial nexus.
Para 3-6: Detailed factual narrative — date, time, place, persons involved, what was done, by whom, how injury caused.

Para 7: Representations made — to SHO, SP, DGP, Home Secretary, Magistrate u/S.175(3) BNSS [S.156(3) CrPC]. Lalita Kumari v. State of UP (2014) 2 SCC 1 — FIR registration mandatory for cognizable offences; refusal contestable.
Para 8: Fundamental rights violated:

Art. 21 — Cite Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) 1 SCC 248; D.K. Basu v. State of WB (1997) 1 SCC 416 (custodial torture guidelines + compensation); Nilabati Behera v. State of Orissa (1993) 2 SCC 746 (compensation for custodial death as constitutional remedy under Art. 32 / 226).
Art. 22 — Arrest procedures — Joginder Kumar v. State of UP (1994) 4 SCC 260; Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273 (arrest checklist for offences ≤ 7 years — now mirrored in S.35(7) BNSS).
Art. 14 — Arbitrary state action; equal protection.
Para 9: For illegal detention short of habeas (where person not in absolute custody but liberty curtailed) — mention this distinction.
Para 10: For custodial torture — D.K. Basu guidelines (now substantially codified in BNSS): arrest memo, medical examination, intimation to relative, etc.

Para 11: For refusal to register FIR — Cite Lalita Kumari v. State of UP (2014) 2 SCC 1: (i) FIR registration mandatory for cognizable; (ii) preliminary inquiry permissible in limited categories (matrimonial, commercial, medical negligence, corruption, abnormal delay). Show steps under S.173(4) BNSS [S.154(3) CrPC] to SP exhausted, and S.175(3) BNSS [S.156(3) CrPC] application before Magistrate.

Para 12: For SIT / CBI transfer — Cite Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1998) 1 SCC 226 (CBI independence); State of WB v. Committee for Protection of Democratic Rights (2010) 3 SCC 571 (HC power to transfer to CBI under Art. 226 without state consent under S.6 DSPE Act); K.V. Rajendran v. Superintendent of Police (2013) 12 SCC 480 (transfer in rare circumstances).

Para 13: For compensation — Public law remedy for violation of FR. Cite Nilabati Behera; D.K. Basu; Saheli v. Commissioner of Police (1990) 1 SCC 422. Distinct from civil tort liability; awarded on principle of constitutional tort.
Para 14: For fake encounter / police excess — Cite PUCL v. State of Maharashtra (2014) 10 SCC 635 (16-point guideline on encounter deaths).
Para 15: Distinction from S.528 BNSS quashing — explicitly note that WP(CRL) does not seek to quash the FIR but to compel investigation / discipline officials / award compensation.
Para 16: Interim relief — production of victim / protection / direction to register FIR.
Prayer — specify writs, compensation amount, disciplinary direction, and CBI/SIT transfer where sought.
Affidavit in support mandatory. Where filed by next friend, affidavit must explain authority.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Life and personal liberty — basis for D.K. Basu / Nilabati Behera doctrines
Protection against arbitrary arrest and detention
When police may arrest (replaces S.41 CrPC) — Arnesh Kumar checklist codified at S.35(7)
Complaint to SP on refusal (replaces S.154(3) CrPC)
Magistrate's power to direct investigation (replaces S.156(3) CrPC)
HC inherent powers — alternative jurisdictional basis
State consent for CBI investigation — HC can dispense under Art. 226 per Committee for Protection of Democratic Rights

filing_checklist: Complaints / representations to authorities (with despatch proof)
Medical reports / post-mortem (for custodial torture / death)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: representations_made must not be empty (exhaustion of remedy)
fundamental_rights_violated must have at least one selected
incident_date must not be in future
If grievance_type = refusal_to_register_fir, fir_status must be 'fir_not_registered_despite_complaint'
If compensation_claimed not empty, amount must be specified
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
Court level restricted to High Court only
